title: A line that senses
hook: A body surface can detect nearby movement.

doesNotKnow: What kind of nearby cue can a fish’s lateral-line system detect?

misconception: The first explanation of an aquatic animal feature must be correct.
objective: What kind of nearby cue can a fish’s lateral-line system detect?

claims.text: What kind of nearby cue can a fish’s lateral-line system detect? The first panel shows a line along the body; the second adds water disturbances next to it. The lateral-line system detects water movement and pressure changes. This drawing is schematic and does not tell us what a particular fish perceives.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/

claims.text: The two panels are simplified schematics, not observations or measurements.
A fish passes close by in dark water. Which cue can reach a neighboring fish’s lateral line? The lateral-line system can detect nearby water motion.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: NOAA Fisheries, fish anatomy and behavior, https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/
